title: Mix-up clinic
theme: a clinic: the words most often taken for each other (đói and đẹp, biết and chào, gặp and khỏe, bớt and đắt), small prices, and reading a price board; Hà Nội's bia hơi corners
intro: A clinic issue: the pairs of words you have mixed up most, side by side, two new words for a street corner (beer, cold), and a price board to read.

feature.title: Fresh beer, every day
feature.dek: Bia hơi is brewed every day, delivered fresh every day, drunk on a plastic stool by evening, and costs less than a bánh mì.
feature.intro: Bia hơi, fresh beer, is found mostly in the North, in small bars and on street corners: a steel keg, a few low tables and a price board on the wall.

beats.text: It is brewed every day and matured only briefly, and each bar gets a fresh batch delivered every day in steel barrels.
It is a very light lager, around 4.1 to 4.3% alcohol, and cheap: a glass typically costs between 10.000₫ and 15.000₫, a fraction of the price of draught or bottled beer in Western-style bars.

The glasses are part of the look: made from recycled glass, with the flaws of the process left clearly visible. Today the rough finish is deliberate, but it began in the 1970s, when the first of these glasses were made quickly from cheap materials.

words.hook: Raise a glass at a street corner: "bee-uh!", one beat, kept level: bia, beer.
words.tip: b is a soft, swallowed b; ia glides from ee to a short uh, in one beat; ngang: level.
words.note: bia: the foaming glass and the keg. bia hơi, fresh draught beer; bia lạnh, cold beer.

words.en: cold (of drinks and food; also of the weather)
words.hook: An ice-cold bottle against your palm: "lie-ng!", low and cut short: lạnh, cold.
words.tip: In Hà Nội anh sounds close to "ine" in "nine" plus ng: lie-ng, one beat. Nặng: low, then a sudden stop.
words.note: lạnh: the frosted bottle. bia lạnh, cold beer; trời lạnh, cold weather. For the winter weather Hà Nội also says rét (issue 11).

grammar.title: ... không? A one-word question
grammar.text: Put không after a word to ask about it: Bia lạnh không? Cold beer? Khỏe không? Are you well? Đói không? Hungry? Answer yes with the word itself (Lạnh! Khỏe! Đói!) and no with không before it (Không đói. Not hungry.).

combos.note: hơi: steam, gas, so 'gas beer'. (hơi also means a bit: hơi đắt, a bit dear.)

check.ask: You have not eaten since the morning. Bà asks if you are hungry. Say your answer aloud first, then pick it.
check.note: Đói quá: so hungry. Đẹp quá: so beautiful (for a view, not your stomach); Biết: I know.

situations.ask: Read the board. You have 10.000₫. Which one costs too much?

situations.who: You, at the bia hơi corner
situations.say: Your friend asks how much the beer is. Read the price of bia hơi off the board.
situations.note: mười lăm: 15 (after mười, năm becomes lăm); nghìn: thousand.

situations.ask: It is a hot evening. The waiter checks you want it cold. What do you answer?
You feel great. Answer your friend.
How much is the iced tea?
situations.note: One number before nghìn is that many thousand: ba nghìn, 3.000. Ba mươi nghìn would be 30.000.

situations.say: Too expensive! (the seller wants 60.000₫ for a hat)
situations.ask: The haggle, turn 1 of 3. Complain about the price.

situations.say: Take some off! (ask for a lower price)
situations.ask: Turn 2 of 3. Ask her to lower it.

situations.note: bốn mươi: forty (mươi = tens), so 40.000; bốn nghìn would be 4.000.

challenge.title: Street challenge
challenge.text: Find a price board today (a tea stall, a bia hơi corner, a phở shop) and read two prices out loud in Vietnamese. At a market stall with no prices, try the two-step: Đắt quá! Bớt đi!
